action_sequence_note: Full from-fresh-reset sequence: 33-action banked L1 prefix (results/experiment_4275) + 61-action L2 solve discovered this session. Verified via arc_solver_kit.reproduce claimed_level=2.
novel_hypothesis_tested: The unexplained 4x4 color-12 object near the bay is a HELPER ROBOT: it advances one tile per player action (any of ACTION1-5), autonomously walks to the nearest loose block, picks it up, carries it to the bay, and deposits it into an empty slot -- a placement that counts toward the win. Cooperative play (robot delivers 3 blocks in parallel while the player hand-carries 2) beats the 80-move single-worker lower bound that made 8 prior probes declare the level a settled dead end. Also newly established: carried blocks occupy the tile on the attachment side and BLOCK movement when their destination cell is solid; contact-highlight outline colors differ by toucher (3=player, 5=robot); timer expiry causes GAME_OVER and a reset that fully restores L2 (placements do NOT persist across episodes); the timer bar drains slightly slower than 1 cell per action (~0.85).
narrative: Replayed the banked 33-action L1 prefix, then investigated the one glyph no prior probe had explained: a solid color-12 4x4 tile near the bay. Standing near it and pressing ACTION5 revealed it moves one tile per player action toward the nearest loose block, picks the block up, carries it to the bay and deposits it into an empty slot -- an autonomous second worker. A first recon episode (deliberately spent) mapped the robot rules, drop geometry (carried block hovers on the pickup side; ACTION5 drops it into the hovered tile), and expiry semantics (GAME_OVER; L2 state fully resets, L1 checkpoint preserved). A second, clean episode split the work: the robot fetched and placed B3->(7,4), B4->(8,4), B1->(7,3) while the player hand-carried B5->(9,4) and B2->(9,3); the fifth drop advanced levels_completed to 2 with ~9 timer cells to spare (61 actions). The prior infeasibility proof (80-move optimistic minimum vs 64-cell timer) was CORRECT under its single-worker assumption -- the level is a two-worker cooperative puzzle, so the route-optimization framing itself was the missed insight. Sequence independently reproduced from a fresh reset via the project reproduction gate (reached_level=2). Bonus recon: L3 is the same delivery puzzle with a vertical dashed barrier separating blocks (left, with player) from the bay (right, with robot).
